correctness.rationale: For every m>=2, p_i>=1, the zero-eigenvalue normalized-Laplacian projector enforces degree equality. Only a root/hub cross-class pair can then match degree, and its exact two-step diagonal normalized-adjacency moments differ by at least one quarter. For same-class pairs, the cited Corollary 8 reduces PST to sibling leaves. A z=0 with z_root=1 and z_leaves=-1/p_i gives a symmetric nonzero eigenvalue-one projector component; e_u-e_v gives an antisymmetric one, so no sibling pair can be strongly cospectral. All boundaries and arbitrary multiplicities covered; exact finite checker separately replays the identities for 360 examples.

originality.rationale: The parameter-unrestricted normalized-Laplacian nonexistence theorem combines an explicit eigenvalue-one strong-cospectrality obstruction for every sibling-leaf pair and a disjoint moment obstruction for every possible cross-class pair. The primary source Corollary 8 only restricts candidates; general twin tests, path-only facts, and a superficially stronger adjacency-Hamiltonian theorem do not state this normalized-Laplacian family exclusion. Semantic publication and result searches revealed no covering implication. General hidden equivalents remain a residual originality risk.
residual_risks: A stronger spectral theorem from the generalized normalized-adjacency literature might imply the exact obstruction without naming this tree family.
Semantic search and inspected primary literature cannot certify globally unique novelty.

value.rationale: The normalized-Laplacian transfer obstruction on arbitrary trees is a motivated open direction. The result excludes every member of a natural depth-two, diameter-four infinite family with arbitrary heterogeneous branch sizes and gives a structural explanation: doubled eigenvalue-one spectral support forbids apparently favorable sibling twins, while degree/moment separation forbids cross-partition candidates. This is more than a fixed instance or a known path example.
